items.title: Ann Rabson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 21, 2007
items.q: that always leads me into that song “Schoolday,” that Chuck Berry song that I do

ctx.x: When you’re in that situation — and I’ve seen you do that — there you are on the piano in front of all these kids and here’s this stack of lyrics, you know, from the third or fourth graders. When you put that in front of you, talking about their grandfather dying, do you wonder, should I share this with the school here.

Yeah. I do wonder. I do wonder. And sometimes there are ones that I don’t. In fact there are some — there have been times where I’ve talked to the teacher afterward. I mean there’s one where they’re being abused by their parents or they feel that they are. There’s a lot where they’re being abused by their siblings, and I mean I’m really into that one. I mean not sexually abused but yeah, there are ones. Mostly they’re pretty silly. And lot of them are about school. In fact, that always leads me into that song…
Right. Getting back to your songwriting for a moment, last night during the concert you said sometimes to the effect that you’re not in control when you’re writing a song.
